Singapore Sports Council (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading

Second Reading13 January 2026 – 14 January 2026 bill-777, bill-778, bill-779

A Bill at Second Reading to amend the Singapore Sports Council Act, expanding SportSG's functions to include physical fitness activities, mind sports and e-sports, and updating its powers over standards, institutions and athlete support.

The Bill expands what is legally recognised as sport to include mind sports and e-sports and physical fitness activities, and gives SportSG powers to set standards and establish athlete-training institutions. It also recognises the Singapore National Paralympic Council as a key partner and increases the maximum SportSG Board size from 15 to 25. The Minister said the changes are to empower SportSG to more effectively administer its role in driving all Singaporeans to live better through sport.

      Verbatim24 words

  • Whether funding for traditional sports will be diluted by support for e-sports and mind sports is not resolved.
  • Whether past athletes will receive retroactive support is not resolved.
  • Whether e-sports and mind sports athletes will have the same access to funding, facilities and national representation pathways as traditional sports athletes is not resolved.
  • Whether the maximum SportSG Board size will remain at 15 or be increased to 25 is not resolved.
  • Whether an ice rink will be built is not resolved.
  • Whether the Singapore National Olympic Council and the Singapore National Paralympic Council will merge is not resolved.
  • Whether accreditation will create a pay-to-play system is not resolved.
  • Whether new standards will impose burdens on small sports organisations and grassroots coaches is not resolved.
  • Whether the Bill will come into force and from what date is not stated.

Parliament debates and votes on motion on Pritam Singh's conduct and suitability as Leader of the Opposition

Motion14 January 2026 motion-2784, motion-2786, motion-2782

A motion moved by the Leader of the House asking Parliament to affirm honesty and integrity, note court and Committee of Privileges findings, express regret at Mr Pritam Singh's conduct, consider him unsuitable to continue as Leader of the Opposition, note implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, and call on MPs to uphold the law.

The transcript states the Motion does not impose penalties or sanctions on Mr Pritam Singh under the PPIPA and does not itself remove the Leader of the Opposition; that designation is for the Prime Minister to decide. The House voted, the Ayes had it, and dissent was recorded for named Members. The Motion also asks the House to note that the High Court judgment and COP findings have implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, to be considered separately.

Adjournment motion on land use, green spaces and the Serangoon River Forest bus depot

Adjournment Motion14 January 2026 matter-adj-2788

An Adjournment Motion in which Dennis Tan called for a rethink of how development and green space trade-offs are assessed, and Minister of State Alvin Tan responded on land use planning and the Serangoon River Forest bus depot.

The record states the planned bus depot at the southern part of the Serangoon area is intended to improve public transport services for residents and bring economic development and jobs closer to homes in Hougang, Sengkang, Defu and Paya Lebar Air Base. LTA has agreed to measures during construction, including hoarding the work site and conducting checks for birds' nests and other wildlife before site clearance. The Minister said the Government will not revisit the matter.

      Verbatim23 words

      Verbatim17 words

    • Dennis Tan said works to develop a bus depot in the middle of part of the Serangoon River Forest between Tampines Road and Buangkok East Drive began a few months ago.

What happens next The Minister said the Government will not revisit the matter; agencies are reviewing potential development plans for the remaining areas along the eastern bank of Sungei Serangoon; LTA has agreed to construction measures. Parliament adjourned at 7.18 pm.

Open questions from this debate (5)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • What specific construction measures has LTA agreed to, and over what period will they apply?
  • What will the agencies' review of potential development plans for the remaining areas along the eastern bank of Sungei Serangoon cover?
  • How will the Government measure whether the planned bus depot improves public transport services for residents?
  • What is the timeline for the progressive development of the site for industrial use?
  • How will the 2030 targets for restoring 80 hectares of habitats and establishing 300 kilometres of nature ways be implemented?
